(This evening through Thursday)...
Issued at 312 PM EDT Thu Oct 29 2026

Rest of this afternoon and tonight...

Widely scattered convection has developed in the last couple of 
hours in northern portions of Indiana. This activity is along the 
edge of the primary theta-e ridge and on the southern periphery of 
an upper trough moving through the Great Lakes. Instability is 
meager at best, with SBCAPE values running 500 j/kg or less in a 
corridor extending SW from this activity into NE IL. CAMs have been 
all over the place with this activity with earlier runs of the HRRR 
more bullish than recent runs, and other CAMs such as the RRFS 
similarly backing off from the 00Z runs. Earlier had bumped up 
pops to chance with added isolated TS given forecast soundings 
showing just enough CAPE to warrant the inclusion. Present satellite 
indications are that southward development is underway across NE IL 
and this activity would move into the northern portions of central 
IN before diminishing between 00-02Z. In the wake of an associated 
cold front, winds will shift to the N-NE ushering in much drier air 
into central IN into early Friday. 

Friday and Friday night... 

Elevated convection will form tonight over the central Plains 
associated with a modest low level jet impinging on a stationary 
boundary. This activity is expected to shift eastward on Friday 
following the low level jet axis while weakening over IA and 
northern IL. Clouds associated with the anvil blow off from 
these storms combined with the large cirrus shield associated with 
southern stream shortwave trough approaching from the SW will lead 
to increasing clouds across central Indiana. In fact, it will be the 
start of many days of less sun that we've seen in quite some time. 
As a result of the increasing cloud cover, and weak CAA associated 
with high pressure centered over the eastern Great Lakes, high temps 
will be 5-10 degrees cooler than Thursday. By Friday night, there 
remains some signal that some of the remnant elevated convection, 
running on almost no instability, will shift into far NW portions of 
central IN. Therefore, have opted to carry low PoPs across this area 
starting after 06Z Saturday. Copious mid-high level clouds across 
the rest of central Indiana will keep overnight lows in the 50s. 

Saturday into Sunday...

Light showers and/or sprinkles will be possible across northern 
portions of central Indiana associated with the remnant elevated 
convection. Otherwise, overcast skies are expected Saturday thanks 
to approaching, yet weakening, lead southern stream shortwave trough 
and copious mid-high level cloud cover. Due to the degree and 
thickness of cloud cover, high temperatures have been notched down a 
cat from previous forecast with temperatures struggling to get out 
of the 60s despite Sat morning lows in the 50s. 

A secondary and stronger shortwave trough (currently just west of 
the Baja CA peninsula) will move E-NE across central Indiana 
Saturday night into Sunday. The OP Euro remains the outlier compared 
to the remainder of model guidance showing generally scattered light 
showers late Saturday night into Sunday morning. With the majority 
of model guidance showing between 0.25 and 0.50 inch of QPF 
(greater south), upgraded PoPs to likely seems the most prudent 
forecast. 

Sunday night into Monday night...

There remains uncertainty in exactly how the phasing of the two 
shortwave troughs will occur over the intermountain west. 
Nonetheless, mid-upper level ridging is expected to commence 
in the wake of the shortwave trough that shifts east of the forecast 
area by early Monday. There is some signal given nearly saturated 
low levels and modest WAA that drizzle or light rain will develop 
and persist during this period so NBM low pops seem reasonable. High 
temps on Monday could easily be 1-2 cats cooler if low clouds and 
drizzle occur through the day.  

Tuesday into Thursday....

The GFS has come in line with other medium range guidance showing a 
more progressive solution with the primary phased trough over the 
plains. Ahead of this trough, ridging will continue to build over 
the eastern CONUS. There is considerable uncertainty regarding how 
strong the ridge will build and therefore the speed of the upper 
trough over the Plains as it pushes towards the MS valley and 
central Indiana. Slower solutions suggest that any precip threat 
will hold off until late Wed, while faster solutions showing precip 
potential as early as Tuesday night. NBM seems overly aggressive with 
likely PoPs early Wednesday given this is still 6 days out. High 
temperatures are likely to be again well above normal in the 70s on 
Tuesday with greater uncertainty for Wed-Thurs based on
